# Morphs and object handoffs

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

One object carries the cut: a pill becomes a window, a shape becomes the next card, a mark becomes the 3D stage. 23 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Shape contracts and hands its outline to the next shot

`dv-shape-match-cut` · transitions · workhorse · energy medium · any

Before each caption cut an outline circle contracts faster (expo-in in its last 3 frames) and the next shot opens on another outline of the same shape; coral circles shrink and cut to a photo with matching thin outlines that contract in place.

- **Build:** Outline as an SVG ring; handoffShot carrying its radius. Anatomy: Outline contracts on an expo-in; the next outline at the same size and place. Sound: A kick on the cut (-17 ms).
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** Last 6 f expo-in; outlines settle 16 f.
- **Use when:** Photo films; chaining captions with one shape motif.
- **Avoid when:** Changing the motif shape between shots.

### Shape match cut

`tr-shape-match-cut` · transitions · workhorse · energy medium · any

The hero shape leaves one shot at a known point and size, and the next shot opens on a matching shape (the mark, the flat plane, the real object) on the same point, so the object's identity carries across a change of world.

- **Build:** MatchCut(frame cut from to outgoing incoming ground) (matchCutState() for the numbers alone). `from` is the outgoing shape's screen box on its last frames (a function of the frame when it moves: toScreen from src/lib/camera.ts, or inkBox from src/lib/measure.ts for type), `to` its rest box in the incoming layout, centred within ±20 px at 0.57-1.3x that size. The incoming shot opens with the shape one outgoing step further along (position and size, size in log space: ratio 1, house) and settles onto its own layout in 36 f, the inherited speed falling to about a third in the first frames and landing with zero speed: where it would carry past its rest it brakes. ratio: 0 matches the box at rest; carry: ['x', 'y'] keeps the centre and opens at the new size; draw the incoming paper as `ground`. Keep motion on both sides: the outgoing shape shrinks 2-4% over its last 4 f on E.in (or a coin turns face-on, rotateY 90 → 10 deg over 22 f on E.out). Match colour, corner radius and stroke weight so only the medium changes (device screen to flat plane, coin emblem to logotype, circle to 3D emblem), and hold the result 12-30 f before it moves on. It declares a morph seam and the camera blur of its fast frames.
- **Primitive:** `fx/MatchCut.MatchCut`, `fx/MatchCut.matchCutState`
- **Timing:** Cut in 0 f. Centre offset ≤ 20 px. Scale ratio 0.57-1.3x. The incoming shot opens one outgoing step on and settles in 36 f, about two thirds of the inherited speed gone in the first frames, at rest with zero speed. Outgoing pre-cut shrink 4 f on E.in. Hold 12-30 f.
- **Use when:** Turning a problem shape into the answer, a device mockup into the bare stage, or a physical object into the mark.
- **Avoid when:** The silhouettes differ (round against tall), so the match cannot be seen. Use a dot relay or a container morph instead.

### The swap hides in a blur peak

`dv-swap-at-blur-peak` · transitions · workhorse · energy medium · any

During a whip or a defocus pulse the content changes where the eye cannot hold it: typed words are replaced mid-whip; a window zooms out into extreme blur and a notification resolves at the same spot; a box goes fully soft and comes back in a new layout; a big blurred blob resolves into the next header; a cut lands blurred and morphs into a near-identical sharp image; a pill becomes a portrait card behind a defocus pulse.

- **Build:** defocusPulse({ at, peakSigma, scaleJump }) + swapAt(peak); whip + swapAt for the whip version. Anatomy: Sharpness falls to near zero for 2-4 f; swap on the softest frame; the new element resolves as a lens would (focus lagging position). Sound: A whoosh and sub on the peak; an impact on the resolve.
- **Primitive:** `fx/SnapZoom`
- **Timing:** 24-60 f; blur peak 4-8 f; resolve tau 6-7 f.
- **Use when:** Any content change inside a fast move.
- **Avoid when:** Swapping on a sharp frame.

### Envelope-matched type cut

`tr-envelope-match-type-cut` · transitions · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting, vertical

A big line hard-cuts to a much smaller, longer line whose words start spread apart so it spans exactly the old line's width, then the gaps close while the sideways drift carries on, so the outer edges of the type survive the cut.

- **Build:** On the cut frame, measure line A's on-screen width W_A and its centre or left edge (measureTracked from src/lib/measure.ts times A's current scale). Lay line B out at rest (cap height 2-3x smaller, more words) and read its natural width W_B, which must be smaller than W_A, and its word positions from measureTracked prefixes. Spread B with an extra gap per word space, g(f) = g0 · (1 − prog(f, 0, 36, E.outSoft)) with g0 = (W_A − W_B)/(n − 1), applied as translateX g · (j − (n − 1)/2) on word j of a centred line (g · j with the left edge pinned for a left-aligned one). Each word keeps its own tracking, so it stays readable while the gaps close. Cut on the act boundary, optionally with one ghost frame of B at 0.65 opacity over A. Both lines carry the same horizontal drift through the cut (A's creep, for example −3.5 px/f), which decays in B over 60 f on E.outSoft, and B may ink in from C.mute to C.ink over 16 f with mixColor.
- **Timing:** Cut in 0 f, or 1 ghost frame at 0.6-0.7 incoming. The gaps close over 36 f on E.outSoft, half done by frame 5. The outermost words travel (W_A − W_B)/2: keep that at or under 160 px so their first frame stays under 20 px/f, or fly them at 0.6 opacity for the first 6 f. Shared drift 3-4 px/f, decaying in B over 60 f. Hold B at least 60 f.
- **Use when:** A big two- or three-word claim hands over to its full sentence or call to action; any big-to-small type change where both lines share a centre or a left edge and the type already drifts sideways.
- **Avoid when:** B is naturally wider than A (use a blur-swap rescale instead), either line is a single word (there are no gaps, so collapse one word's tracking instead), or the alignment changes across the cut.

### Object implodes into a point or vortex

`dv-implode-to-point` · transitions · accent · energy medium · launch, sting

A ring spirals inward into a single bright point with the caption fading inside it; a totem shrinks under the lead subject and the next frame is a short soft swirling ring that births the title; a white disc dissolves from the inside out.

- **Build:** Build: Implode(at r x y color kind="spiral"|"vortex"|"hole") (a custom stage layer): spiral: the ring coils inward on M.squeeze, posed every 5 f (radius 1, .79, .60, .17, then a point held 6 f); vortex: three tightening arcs (12 f); hole: a ground-coloured hole grows in the disc while it dims (18 f). Anatomy: Spiral radius 369 -> 291 -> 223 -> 64 -> point on twos accelerating; swirl of 2-3 soft arcs for 6 f; an inner hole growing 35 -> 218 px while the disc dims. Sound: A pop or a spoken word; no hit for the spiral. Materials: Three constructions. Burn-out: a dark soft hole grows from the disc's centre (radius 12 -> 75 % of the disc) while the outer edge defocuses 0 -> 14 px and the luma drops to about 13 %, in 18 f. Swirl: the dot grid behind bends into waves curling round the target (displacement up to 20-40 px, falling off over 400 px, roughly doubling each frame) and a trail is sucked in as a thin tongue, 8 f into the vortex. Snake: the ring's tail erases while its head keeps drawing past 360 deg on a falling radius, on twos (20 f), the caption fading under the coil.
- **Materials:** Three constructions. Burn-out: a dark soft hole grows from the disc's centre (radius 12 -> 75 % of the disc) while the outer edge defocuses 0 -> 14 px and the luma drops to about 13 %, in 18 f. Swirl: the dot grid behind bends into waves curling round the target (displacement up to 20-40 px, falling off over 400 px, roughly doubling each frame) and a trail is sucked in as a thin tongue, 8 f into the vortex. Snake: the ring's tail erases while its head keeps drawing past 360 deg on a falling radius, on twos (20 f), the caption fading under the coil.
- **Timing:** 12-20 f.
- **Use when:** Ending a section on a point; birthing a title from an object.
- **Avoid when:** Long vortices (keep under 12 f).

### Outgoing scene melts by defocus under the next

`dv-defocus-melt-under` · transitions · accent · energy calm · any

The background layer blurs, smears and darkens away while the next graphic draws on top; a soft blob rises from the bottom while the shot defocuses and tints; the outgoing headline lifts 22 px in one frame and defocuses as a tilted card rises over it.

- **Build:** Dive() with a short occluder, or RackFocus levels on the outgoing layer while the next draws. Anatomy: Defocus on an ease-in, a darken or tint, a one-frame lift; the incoming element sharp from its first frame. Sound: A glockenspiel note; the voice phrase start. Materials: Before the colour finale, the photo is re-coloured into the gradient's palette as it blurs away: a faint pale blob breathes up from one corner (10 f), a second hue rises in its place (10 f), then the rest flood in from the other side and, on the same frame, the photo is gradient-mapped (dark -> deep hue, mid -> pink, light -> warm), blurred about 150 px and fades out over 16 f.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Dive`
- **Materials:** Before the colour finale, the photo is re-coloured into the gradient's palette as it blurs away: a faint pale blob breathes up from one corner (10 f), a second hue rises in its place (10 f), then the rest flood in from the other side and, on the same frame, the photo is gradient-mapped (dark -> deep hue, mid -> pink, light -> warm), blurred about 150 px and fades out over 16 f.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** 10-25 f.
- **Use when:** Layered scene changes where the new element arrives on top.
- **Avoid when:** Fading without defocus (it reads as a crossfade).

### Parts detach and reassemble into a big shape

`dv-parts-reassemble-shape` · transitions · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

The type is cut away and its coloured tag fills detach as bars, rotate and slide into a giant arrow that fills the panel, then exit.

- **Build:** assembleState with parts given explicit from offsets and rotations. Anatomy: Bars rotate and translate to target slots; quart-in exit. Sound: None needed.
- **Timing:** Assemble 30 f; exit 18 f.
- **Use when:** Turning labels into a direction (next, forward, go).
- **Avoid when:** Too many parts (more than about 8).

### Pill breathes into a window

`tr-pill-breath-window` · transitions · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, update · also `dv-pill-breath`

An image in a pill mask stretches, holds, contracts into the cut at its fastest, and the next shot opens as a window from the pill's own box, growing in a few held steps while the old frame steps back.

- **Build:** pillBreath(f, { start, from, to, h, stretch, hold, contract, end }) drives the pill's width; cut on .cut. Then windowStep({ frame, start: cut, rects: [pillBox, mid, large], radius: [h / 2], oldScale: [1, 1, 0.94, 0.86, 0.86], cadence: 16 }).
- **Timing:** Stretch 44 f on E.snapOut (90 % in the first 16), hold 12 f, contract 22 f on E.launchIn to 0.86 of the width (the last step the fastest); window 4 held steps on 16 fps (about 15 f at 60 fps).
- **Use when:** A framed image or card should become the next scene.
- **Avoid when:** The image is small text (it must read before it moves).

### Side elements gather toward the centre into the cut

`dv-gather-to-centre` · transitions · accent · energy medium · any

Stickers and scraps around a headline slide 45-100 px toward it while their scale holds, fastest on the last frame before the transition.

- **Build:** MorphChain gather phase (linear drift then M.squeeze) or a simple E.buildIn toward the centre. Anatomy: Strong ease-in; peak 7 px/f on the last frame. Sound: The downbeat at the cut.
- **Timing:** 48 f.
- **Use when:** Before a cut or a pixelate on a collage.
- **Avoid when:** Gathering that settles.

### Tags dissolve through low-res pixels into dots

`dv-pixel-dissolve-to-dots` · transitions · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

Tags breathe wider slowly, then dissolve as pale low-resolution pixel blocks into two small dots that hold.

- **Build:** Pixelate out-phase on the tags, then two dots via HardStep. Anatomy: Breathe +3.8 %; dissolve 5 f; dots hold 8 f. Sound: A plucked note.
- **Timing:** 65 f in all.
- **Use when:** Ending a data moment into a minimal mark.
- **Avoid when:** Large blocks.

### A soft panel flies through the camera

`dv-fly-through-panel` · transitions · signature · energy medium · any

The card recedes while a large frosted white panel scales toward the camera and fills the frame, then the next scene comes out of it.

- **Build:** Dive(occluder={softPanel}) with the panel scaled from 0.6 to 3 on E.buildIn. Anatomy: Card to 0.86; panel fills (centre luma 188 -> 248); next scene resolves. Sound: A glockenspiel note; a level dip before.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Dive`
- **Conditions:** glass as a material with real frost or refraction, not a default card style
- **Timing:** 48 f: 14 f up, 22 f down.
- **Use when:** A soft, bright transition between stage scenes.
- **Avoid when:** Dark films (the panel reads as a flash).

### A straight row curls into a ring

`dv-ring-curl` · transitions · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

A strip of tiles starts rotating with acceleration and both ends wrap around (the leader over the top, the tail along the bottom) until the row closes into a ring, on the kick after a short silence.

- **Build:** Build: RingCurl(at n pitch x y render={(i) =) tile}> (a custom stage layer): every tile rides a curve bent from the row into a circle of the same length by its arc length (32 f on E.buildIn: it closes at speed), the whole turning 45 deg, then still turning and slowing (tau 10 f). Anatomy: Arc-length parametrisation: tiles move along a path that morphs from a line to a circle while the whole rotates. Sound: A kick exactly on the fastest frame after a 0.35 s silence.
- **Timing:** 32 f on an ease-in; the ring closes 4-6 f after the fastest frame.
- **Use when:** Turning a list of things into a cycle or an ecosystem.
- **Avoid when:** Fewer than 5 tiles.

### Letters replaced by product objects

`dv-letters-become-objects` · transitions · signature · energy medium · launch

The letters of a word are swapped in place for product renders (laptop, headphones, camera) with soft contact shadows, the row spreads, then implodes.

- **Build:** Recipe: Letters positions as anchors, Three.js textured quad per letter with a FloatShadow. Anatomy: Per letter a render at the letter's box; spread circ-out; implode 13 f. Sound: None needed.
- **Timing:** Swap 10 f; spread 90 f; implode 13 f.
- **Use when:** Commerce, product catalogues.
- **Avoid when:** Without real product renders.

### Old words step into depth, new words step out

`dv-z-swarm-swap` · transitions · signature · energy high · launch, sting

Copies of the old words shrink into depth in steps while copies of the new line grow out of depth along the same axis, jitter for a few frames and lock; trails fade.

- **Build:** Build: ZSwarm(at x y old={line} next={line}) (a custom stage layer): the old line steps back -0.15 scale per 30 fps frame (6 steps), the new one steps out from 0.2 by +0.10 (8 steps, 4 f behind), each step leaving two fading copies (45 %, 20 %); the new line jitters 6 f (6 px) and locks: 26 f in all. Anatomy: Old -0.15 scale a frame for 6 f, new +0.10 a frame for 8 f, linear; jitter 4 f; trails of each step fading. Sound: A punchy impact at full scale.
- **Timing:** 26 f at 60 fps.
- **Use when:** A techno title change; a hook line swap.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films.

### One object carries the cut

`ps-oner-morph-chain` · transitions · signature · energy medium · launch, update, feature, loop

A chip, card or dot from the outgoing shot gathers, swells and becomes the next word or panel at its own size; the camera carries the swell's growth on into the new content, so the film moves on without a cut.

- **Build:** Write the object's states as boxes (x, y, w, h, radius, fill) with blur, opacity and a content index; join them with windows { from, to, ease }. A one-frame window on CHAIN_STEP is the designed swap: the next content appears at the object's pre-swell size. Render MorphChain(frame states windows){[a, b]}</MorphChain> inside the world the camera moves, and start a camera push on E.glideOut on the swap frame.
- **Timing:** Gather 16-22 f (a linear drift, then M.squeeze), hold 2-4 f, swell +40-60 % over 12-24 f on M.swell straight into the swap; a collapse under blur 16-20 f (ease-in, blur to 12-20 px at 1080p while it fades). Hand-offs every 8-32 f.
- **Use when:** The outgoing shot ends on a small object that means the next thing (a totem that becomes the feature's name, a chip that becomes a panel).
- **Avoid when:** Nothing on screen relates to the next shot: a morph between unrelated things reads as a gimmick.

### Small element grows into the next scene

`dv-grow-into-next-scene` · transitions · signature · energy medium · any

A marker badge, a single cell, an inline photo pill or a lit monolith grows (exponentially or on an expo in-out) until it is the next scene; a totem can become a porthole the next subject rises into.

- **Build:** growThrough({ start, frames, from, to }) (E.buildIn); the porthole is Iris at the totem's size with the next subject masked inside. Anatomy: Growth x1.15 a frame while the centre moves to the frame centre; x2.44 in one frame for a cell; an inline pill accelerating its own growth in the last 7 f of a push. Sound: Water drops then a sub-drop; an onset at the cover. Materials: A notch in a custom glyph of the wordmark becomes a slit that opens into the next shot: an 8 px sliver appears exactly in the notch, then widens into a photo band whose height grows 4, 6, 12, 20, 35, 50, 75, 95, 140 px (one value a frame at 30 fps, width leading height by about 8 f) while the wordmark greys and fades to 20 %.
- **Materials:** A notch in a custom glyph of the wordmark becomes a slit that opens into the next shot: an 8 px sliver appears exactly in the notch, then widens into a photo band whose height grows 4, 6, 12, 20, 35, 50, 75, 95, 140 px (one value a frame at 30 fps, width leading height by about 8 f) while the wordmark greys and fades to 20 %.
- **Timing:** 14-48 f; the cover frame is the cut.
- **Use when:** Opening a detail into its world; from a chip in a sentence to its full picture.
- **Avoid when:** Growth that slows before the cover (it must accelerate into the frame).

### Text collapses into an object

`dv-text-collapses-to-object` · transitions · signature · energy medium · any

A finished line stops being text and becomes a thing: both ends rush to the centre while it thickens into a short fat pill (area kept), it is replaced by one solid bar of its size that slides into a chat pill, it blooms and squeezes into a small pill, it heats and collapses to a few dots that draw an icon, blocks advance and eat it from its end, or it is erased in chunks while a square grows in the cleared space.

- **Build:** MorphChain(states={[line, bar|pill|dots, object]}) with a collapse window (ease-in, blur 12-20 px) and a one-frame CHAIN_STEP swap. Anatomy: Width 258 -> 66 px, height 10 -> 28 (area constant) on a cubic-in; a solid bar for 3 f; dots for 2 f then strokes; chunks of 2-3 letters a frame. Sound: A lead-in to a kick; a kick on the eat; a click on the erase. Materials: The object can be a flip-book pixel sprite filled with a grainy two-hue gradient (cells about 40 px, gradient at 135 deg, monochrome grain at about 4 %, rim cells in a deeper shade), one drawing every 4 f, pushing the next word aside as it widens.
- **Materials:** The object can be a flip-book pixel sprite filled with a grainy two-hue gradient (cells about 40 px, gradient at 135 deg, monochrome grain at about 4 %, rim cells in a deeper shade), one drawing every 4 f, pushing the next word aside as it widens.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** 10-50 f; the collapse itself 6-16 f.
- **Use when:** Moving from a statement to the product (the line becomes the input, the totem, the icon).
- **Avoid when:** Collapsing a line before it has been read.

### The full stop becomes the next object

`dv-period-becomes-object` · transitions · signature · energy medium · launch, sting

The last mark of a sentence (a period, a signature's dot, a hero point, a bar) turns into the next thing: it scales into a shaded ball and drips a stem that becomes the next shot's line; pops oversized, swells and drops onto a planet; grows exponentially to frame centre and cuts to an inverted frame at the same size; swells into a planet disc; or a bar retracts into a sphere that falls into the end card.

- **Build:** MorphChain from the period's measured box (document.fonts.ready) to a ball, then growThrough or a drop on E.buildIn; the full-stop zoom via zoomThrough with an inverted next frame. Anatomy: Pop that starts oversized (r 14 -> 6.6 px), swell on cubic-in, drop on a quart-in with gravity (73 px/f); exponential growth x1.10 -> x1.26 a frame; a stem with 5 % overshoot. Sound: An onset on the pop, a stage pop and kicks on the drop; voice names the next thing. Materials: The swollen dot is first a flat, soft-edged disc with grain (edge feather 10 % of the radius, grain about 6 levels that changes on held frames) for 12 f, then real footage develops into it from one edge (a diagonal mask in 2-3 steps on twos) until it is a photograph.
- **Materials:** The swollen dot is first a flat, soft-edged disc with grain (edge feather 10 % of the radius, grain about 6 levels that changes on held frames) for 12 f, then real footage develops into it from one edge (a diagonal mask in 2-3 steps on twos) until it is a photograph.
- **Timing:** 28-75 f in all; pop 20 f, swell 10 f, drop 17-25 f.
- **Use when:** Ending a statement into the next scene; into the end card.
- **Avoid when:** Punctuation the viewer has not noticed (give it a beat).

### Whole frame collapses into a chip or card

`dv-collapse-to-chip` · transitions · signature · energy medium · any

The entire image shrinks fast under heavy blur into a small rounded chip; a design shrinks into a card on paper and cuts to it living on a billboard; a collage collapses into an 3D emblem tile; a lockup collapses while a strip of tiles grows from its centre glyph; a sheet collapses in hard steps to one cell that turns green and sinks.

- **Build:** collapse(f, { start, frames, square, into }) from MorphChain; stepped variant via HardStep widths. Anatomy: Collapse 10 f (about 230 px/f) with corner rounding and blur, then a linear shrink, a brief sharpening, a squeeze; stepped variant 835 -> 689 -> 413 -> 309 -> 277 px over 7 f. Sound: A boom; a drum (+39 ms); a sub-bass. Materials: A hairline outline (1 px white at 25 %, radius 8, inset 2 % from the text block) appears round the last words in 4 f and contracts with the photo into the chip (image corners 0 -> 40 px, extreme blur); the chip is a live window: a crop of the same photo keeps drifting about 0.75 px/f and lightens about 40 % over 70 f inside it while its label fades in 6 f.
- **Materials:** A hairline outline (1 px white at 25 %, radius 8, inset 2 % from the text block) appears round the last words in 4 f and contracts with the photo into the chip (image corners 0 -> 40 px, extreme blur); the chip is a live window: a crop of the same photo keeps drifting about 0.75 px/f and lightens about 40 % over 70 f inside it while its label fades in 6 f.
- **Timing:** 13-64 f.
- **Use when:** Packing a whole scene into one object of the next scene.
- **Avoid when:** Collapsing on an ease-out (it must accelerate).

### Zoom into a letter until it fills the frame

`dv-zoom-through-glyph` · transitions · signature · energy high · launch, sting

The middle letters of a word scale up inside their own box at a constant x1.42 a frame (x8 in 6 f) until one glyph part fills the frame, then a match cut to a label box of the same shape.

- **Build:** zoomThrough({ factor: 8, frames: 14, box: glyphBox }) or TypeMask() push; handoffShot carrying k. Anatomy: Constant log rate; the glyph's box as the cover target; label expo-out after the cut. Sound: A drip or bubble on the cover.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** Zoom 14 f; label 22 f.
- **Use when:** From a word into its meaning; a title into the first scene.
- **Avoid when:** Letters with thin strokes (the fill reads as a flash).

### Letters spread and double while the ground warms

`dv-letters-spread-ghost` · typography in motion · accent · energy high · launch, sting

A stat's letters spread apart and get doubled outline ghosts while the ground warms to the accent in 4 frames.

- **Build:** Recipe: Letters tracking out + one outline copy offset per letter; ground via HardStep tween. Anatomy: Tracking out, outline ghost copies offset, ground colour step. Sound: None needed.
- **Timing:** 20 f; colour 10 f.
- **Use when:** Leaving a statistic.
- **Avoid when:** Warm grounds in a cool brand.

### Tiles pass through a wireframe look

`dv-xray-wireframe-pass` · colour and light · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

Collage tiles turn white with thin dark outlines in 2 frames (a structural x-ray), the outlines and caption turn a pale tint and fade to white.

- **Build:** HardStep to an outline version of each tile (a pre-drawn stroke layer), then a fade to the ground. Anatomy: Two-frame switch, then a tint, then white. Sound: A whoosh.
- **Timing:** 5 + 10 f.
- **Use when:** A transition that reveals structure.
- **Avoid when:** Busy tiles.

### Flat shape builds into a 3D object

`dv-flat-to-3d-construct` · depth and 3d · signature · energy medium · launch, sting

A flat outline grows into a solid: a triangle gains a fourth vertex out of plane and turns as a wireframe, its faces fill one after another; a square outline grows into a tumbling cube; a pyramid forms in halves around a hero; flat cards morph into glossy 3D balls while a ring spins.

- **Build:** Recipe: Three.js Object3D hierarchy faces with stroke-only first, fills on per-face onsets. Anatomy: Wireframe 1-2 px; faces fill 2-3 f apart; tumble 180 deg slow-in slow-out. Sound: A note on the first face fill; a celesta with the core glow. Materials: Construction hairlines stay drawn on top of the shaded solid: every edge, including back edges seen through a clear face, remains a 1 px light line at about 70 % with a non-scaling stroke through the whole beauty hold.
- **Materials:** Construction hairlines stay drawn on top of the shaded solid: every edge, including back edges seen through a clear face, remains a 1 px light line at about 70 % with a non-scaling stroke through the whole beauty hold.
- **Conditions:** glass as a material with real frost or refraction, not a default card style
- **Timing:** Construct 18-72 f.
- **Use when:** A product about structure, models, building; a hero object reveal.
- **Avoid when:** Glossy 3D in a flat plane film.
